function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a file in the remote Workspace. Read before editing an existing file.

file_path.description: Path relative to the saved Session working directory in its remote Workspace. Never use the Harness host path.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write a file in the remote Workspace. Read before overwriting an existing file. Write/Edit preimages are backed up. External or Shell changes to tracked content or permissions block further Write/Edit in the same prompt and block undo. A new Write/Edit prompt must validate a fresh backup before accepting those changes.

file_path.description: Path relative to the saved Session working directory in its remote Workspace. Never use the Harness host path.

function.name: edit
function.description: Replace exact text in a remote Workspace file that you have read. Write/Edit preimages are backed up. External or Shell changes to tracked content or permissions block further Write/Edit in the same prompt and block undo. A new Write/Edit prompt must validate a fresh backup before accepting those changes.

file_path.description: Path relative to the saved Session working directory in its remote Workspace. Never use the Harness host path.

function.name: run_shell_command
function.description: Run a command in the saved Workspace working directory. Complete stdout and stderr are retained; the model receives a bounded preview. With is_background the command runs detached: the call returns a durable handle at once, the process outlives the turn and holds its Runtime until it exits, and its output lands as a task Artifact. Shell file mutations are not backed up. Changing tracked file content or permissions can cause subsequent Write/Edit and undo conflicts.

function.name: monitor
function.description: Watch a shell command in the saved Workspace working directory and receive its stdout lines as observations while it runs. Observations aggregate by one-second-or-longer debounce windows, so `max_events` counts windows, not lines; `idle_timeout_ms` bounds the silent stretch between windows ending the watch. The watch is admitted only on Sessions whose Monitor path is enabled.

function.name: send_message
function.description: Send a message to another member of your team by name, to every other member at once (to: "*"), or to the team leader (to: "parent"). Member messages travel through the leader, which answers with each recipient's outcome; a running member receives the message as its next input once its current turn ends, and a member that has finished, ended or is being stopped is not reached. There is no inline reply: the recipient answers you with send_message naming you, and the leader's reply arrives as your next instruction. A message is not a board change: record work with the task tools.

to.description: A member name, "*" for every other member, or "parent" for the team leader.

function.name: task_list
function.description: List your team board, optionally filtered, followed by each member with the state of its current run — the board and the roster as your leader holds them. Board changes are not pushed to you: read the board again when you need the current state.

blockedBy.description: Filter for tasks still blocked by this task number.

function.name: task_create
function.description: Create a pending task on your team board. The leader records it and answers with the new task number. Members are not told about board changes: put new work for another member in your final answer, or ask the leader to hand it out.

activeForm.description: Present tense label for UI (e.g., "Running tests").

function.name: task_update
function.description: Update a board task: status, owner, subject, description, active form, metadata or dependencies; set status to "deleted" to remove it. Status, owner, subject and description change only on a task you own or that has no owner, and edges only reach such tasks; activeForm and metadata change on any task; owner may be only your own name or "" to unassign, and moving an unowned task to in_progress makes you its owner. A task in progress needs an owner. The answer is the revised task, or the refusal.

taskId.description: Number of the task to update, as "3" or "#3".

owner.description: New owner: your own name, or an empty string to unassign.

metadata.description: Metadata to merge. Set a key to null to delete it.

addBlocks.description: Numbers of the tasks this task blocks.

addBlockedBy.description: Numbers of the tasks that block this task.
